key_insight: THz time-domain spectroscopy can non-destructively identify and quantify grain-boundary defect species in organic halide perovskite thin films by reading their unique terahertz fingerprints.
engineering_relevance: This enables a closed-loop quality-control and passivation workflow for perovskite solar cells, linking defect diagnosis directly to performance improvement.
method: Measure 0.3–3.0 THz spectra of device-relevant perovskite films.
Match intrinsic phonons and grain-boundary-localized defect modes to a THz fingerprint library.
Use oscillator-strength analysis to quantify defect concentration and guide passivation.
evidence_signal: Across four compositions, the SVE-specific 1.58 THz absorption in MAPbI3 scales linearly with XPS-measured CH3NH2 defect concentration, supporting THz-TDS as a direct defect meter.
watch_item: The approach depends on a sufficiently complete THz fingerprint library and may need careful calibration to separate overlapping defect signals in complex films.
paper_title: Terahertz Time-Domain Spectroscopy as a Universal Defect Fingerprinting Tool for Organic Halide Perovskite Solar Cells
